speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with a recent low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To help narrow down the cause, could you tell me exactly how many days ago these symptoms started?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The timeline of symptoms—fever and upper respiratory symptoms starting a week ago, followed by a facial rash sparing the nasolabial folds (perioral area)—is highly suggestive of a specific viral exanthem. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on her face and arms, specifically if it looks like a fine, pink, sandpaper-like texture?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.
